name: Datum Plot
tagline: Analyse data and make publication-ready graphs: statistics, regression, curve fitting and page layouts, in one app for Windows.
for: Scientists, researchers, lab teams and students.
about: Datum Plot keeps data, analyses and graphs linked. Type or paste data into a table, choose an analysis, and the results and the graph follow; change a value and everything updates.

It covers the statistics most lab and research work needs, from t-tests and ANOVA to regression and curve fitting, explains each result in plain words with ready methods text, and makes figures ready for a journal: multi-panel layouts at journal sizes, exported as PNG, TIFF, SVG, PDF or EPS. Python runs inside the app, with nothing else to install, and a built-in console lets you run your own code on the data.

steps.title: Enter the data
steps.text: Choose a table for your kind of data and type, paste or import it (CSV, TXT, .xlsx, .pzfx, plate readers, many runs at once).

steps.title: Analyse
steps.text: Pick a test or a fit; the results, P values and methods text open on a results sheet linked to the data, and fits are drawn on the graph.

steps.title: Graph and export
steps.text: Style the graph, lay out the figure and export it at journal size.

highlights: A linked chain: data tables → analyses → results → graphs → layouts. Change a value and every result and graph updates.

Data tables for every kind of experiment (XY, groups, two factors, counts, survival, nested, many variables) and worksheets with units and column formulas that update as the data change; dates and times in the X column, drawn on date axes.
Import CSV, TXT, .xlsx and .pzfx files, plate readers and many runs at once; large data sets stay quick.

Statistics: descriptive, normality, outliers, t-tests, nonparametric tests, one- and two-way ANOVA with multiple comparisons, repeated measures and mixed-effects models, multiple t-tests with false discovery rates and volcano plots, nested t-tests and ANOVA, contingency tables, correlation, power, Bland-Altman, ROC, and survival analysis (Kaplan-Meier, log-rank, hazard ratios); three-way ANOVA, ANCOVA, agreement (Cohen's kappa, McNemar) and bootstrap confidence intervals.

Linear regression and curve fitting with a model library or your own equation, global fits and model comparison, smoothing splines; multiple, logistic and Poisson regression, principal components and clustering on tables of many variables.
Matrices and 3D: contour maps, heat maps, 3D surfaces and 3D scatter, vector fields, polar, ternary, bubble, radar and waterfall graphs, and surface fits (plane, quadratic, cubic, 2D Gaussian).
Peaks and signals: find peaks above a baseline, fit Gaussian, Lorentzian or Voigt peaks, Fourier spectra and filters, wavelet scalograms and spectrograms.
Quality: control charts (individuals, X̄–R, X̄–S, p) with capability, and two-level factorial designs with their effects.
Materials testing: tensile tests, Weibull strength, Arrhenius activation energies, S–N fatigue curves, and DSC/TGA thermal analysis (onsets, enthalpies, mass loss).
Publication graphs: error bars (mean or median), axis breaks (XY and column graphs), a second Y axis, annotations, colour-blind-safe colours, multi-panel figures and insets.

Page layouts at journal sizes, posters and slides; graphs pasted into documents, slides and workbooks that open again in Datum Plot with a double-click (Windows); export as PNG or TIFF (with CMYK), SVG, PDF or EPS, every graph as slides (.pptx or .odp), or a document with graphs, results and methods (.docx or .odt); tables and results as a workbook (.xlsx or .ods).
Interactive graphs: zoom, pan, drag notes, exclude points with a right-click, and the statistics of any region.
A Python console inside the app, with your tables as pandas DataFrames and a built-in guide; your own saved analyses, analysis templates, batch processing and notebook export.
Safe and sturdy: projects never run code, saves never leave half-written files, damaged files open or explain why, and updates are checked against their checksums.
A step-by-step guide with pictures in English, Chinese and French (Help › Guide), blank starts with or without a graph, and over twenty sample projects to learn from, grouped by subject.
Free and open source (MIT), Windows first, installs in seconds with Python inside, and updates itself.
Read the points of a published graph from its picture into a table.
